title: I Became a Legend after My 10 Year-Long Last Stand
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: The mage Luck stays behind between dimensions so his party can escape a demon horde, and holds the line alone for ten years. Returning as a forgotten 'Great Sage' in a changed world, he turns down noble life, renames himself Lock and starts over as a rookie adventurer, taking in an orphaned apprentice and befriending a werewolf hunter (Wikipedia; Comikey blurb via AniList; AnimeFeminist).
life_message: Sacrifice for friends is noble, and after it a person deserves the freedom to start again on their own terms.

content.note: Battles with demons and vampires; a tribe's massacre in backstory (Wikipedia); 'Fantasy Gore' warning (AnimeFeminist).
AniList Ecchi genre and Female Harem 46, Nudity 20; MangaDex suggestive; anime reviewer says it avoids 'icky tropes' (to verify for manga).
Difficulty reintegrating after a decade-long fight (AnimeFeminist).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Gods, sacred beasts and a clergy in the world (Wikipedia).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival battle gives way to a chosen new life.

folkways.japan: The phrase 'leave this to me and go ahead' is a stock Japanese heroic line that the title turns into a premise.

delivery.evidence: AnimeFeminist praises a warm, uncynical tone and the cost of reintegration shown through events, not lectures.
delivery.note: Themes of sacrifice and starting over are carried by Luck's choices; sources describe no character set up to argue the other side.

winners_losers: Luck and his friends prosper and reunite; demons and vampires are defeated. Sympathy goes to loyalty and fresh starts.
